hypothesis: Reproduce the purchased Hixton indicator as a causal closed-candle baseline on the existing ten-coin Binance Spot universe, without pair-specific tuning, then measure all ten independent 250-USDT diagnostics and the shared 250-USDT 3x80 portfolio.
development_window: rolling 3y ending at first clean execution
validation_window: same exact clean execution; diagnostics only
reason_accepted_or_rejected: MEASUREMENT BASELINE - NO PROMOTION DECISION BEFORE RESULTS
notes: Fresh isolated branch. No V12.33 entry/exit filters or pair-specific rules are allowed in this baseline. Pine ta.sma and ta.atr/RMA semantics are implemented explicitly.
change_summary: New independent Hixton family: VIDYA 10/20 smoothed by Pine-compatible SMA15, Pine-compatible ATR200 x2 bands, long on upper crossover, exit on lower crossunder; fixed 80-USDT stake; no pyramiding.
acceptance_criteria: Complete all ten 3y individual diagnostics with valid 1m/15m/1h/4h data audit and then complete the chronological shared 3x80 portfolio. Record results without post-result parameter changes.
lessons: Do not infer profitability before the clean run; any later variant must be materially different and receive a new fingerprint.
next_experiment: After baseline results, decide separately per coin whether Hixton is useful unchanged, as a filter, or should be rejected.

hypothesis: The original Hixton motor has positive raw trend capture on the first completed V1 diagnostics but loses too much to false breakouts, fees and late lower-band exits. A shared 1h VIDYA context guard plus an earlier 15m VIDYA midline exit should improve average edge per trade without pair-specific tuning.
validation_window: all ten individual diagnostics plus shared 3x80 portfolio
reason_accepted_or_rejected: REJECTED - shared portfolio lost about 68% and the midline exit destroyed large trend winners
notes: Complete V2 trade analysis found two separate issues: the 15m midline exit cut the few large winners that pay for a trend-following system, and the intended 1h VIDYA slope check was calculated after informative forward-fill by comparing adjacent 15m rows rather than native hourly values.
change_summary: Keep original 15m Hixton flip-up, require completed 1h close above a non-falling 1h Hixton VIDYA, exit on 15m close cross below Hixton VIDYA while green, retain original lower-band flip-down fallback; no pyramiding and no ROI target.
acceptance_criteria: Against V1, reduce fee drag and severe giveback while improving net P/L and profit factor across the ten-pair set; reject if gains are isolated to one or two coins or shared 250-USDT portfolio robustness worsens materially.
result_summary: 10 individual V2 diagnostics all negative; shared portfolio 250 -> about 79.99 USDT, 688 trades, PF 0.668. V1/V2 matched-entry analysis showed the guard-selected ETH and XRP trades would have been slightly positive with the original Hixton exit, while the V2 midline exit turned them materially negative.
lessons: Do not use an unconditional VIDYA-midline exit for this Hixton trend follower. Compute informative-timeframe slope before merging/forward-filling into 15m. Preserve large trend winners until evidence supports a profit-protection mechanism.

hypothesis: The V2 entry guard showed useful selection on matched V1 entries, but V2 was invalidated by a destructive midline exit and an incorrectly evaluated forward-filled 1h slope. Computing VIDYA slope inside the native 1h dataframe and restoring the original lower-band Hixton exit should preserve the guard's filtering benefit while allowing large trend winners to run.
validation_window: all ten individual diagnostics plus completed shared 3x80 portfolio
reason_accepted_or_rejected: NOT PROMOTED - large improvement versus V2 but shared portfolio remained negative with severe drawdown
notes: Ten V3A individual runs: DOGE +40.39 PF1.187; XRP +32.74 PF1.171; TRX +11.47 PF1.083; ETH -4.81 PF0.969; SOL -16.99 PF0.930; BTC -28.32 PF0.816; LINK -33.47 PF0.844; BNB -59.11 PF0.704; BCH -65.87 PF0.716; LTC -79.62 PF0.597. The later completed shared portfolio had 1321 trades, 394 wins, 927 losses, final balance 177.55 USDT, PF 0.9449 and 61.34% max drawdown. Pair contributions inside that shared run were SOL +46.46, XRP +43.34, DOGE +32.91, ETH +27.02, LINK +1.90, BTC -28.51, TRX -37.55, LTC -49.15, BNB -52.62 and BCH -56.24 USDT.
change_summary: Keep purchased VIDYA10/momentum20/SMA15/ATR200x2 motor and 15m flip-up; calculate 1h hixton_vidya_rising on native 1h candles before informative merge; require completed 1h close above VIDYA plus native 1h non-falling VIDYA; exit only on original 15m lower-band flip-down.
acceptance_criteria: Must materially beat V2 on net P/L and PF without losing the large winners observed under the original Hixton exit. Evaluate all ten independent 3y diagnostics and the real shared 250-USDT max-3x80 portfolio before promotion.
result_summary: V3A substantially improved V2 and made DOGE/XRP/TRX positive as standalones. Gross pre-fee edge remained positive for eight of ten pairs. The shared portfolio nevertheless lost 72.45 USDT and reached 61.34% drawdown, so V3A is a diagnostic parent rather than a production candidate.
lessons: Original lower-band exit is preferable to both V2 midline and V4 profit-floor exits. Remaining work should preserve V3A winners and change only weak pair routes rather than applying a universal early-profit mechanism.

hypothesis: V3A restored the correct trend-following exit and exposed the remaining failure mode: many losing trades first reached a meaningful positive excursion. A conservative pair-specific fee-covering floor activated only after a rounded, volatility-sensitive peak-profit threshold should prevent profitable trades from round-tripping below their entry-plus-exit fees without clipping trends. ETH should omit the 1h rising-slope clause because matched original-exit evidence shows that clause removed a profitable ETH subset.
validation_window: all ten individual diagnostics complete; uploaded archive caught shared V4 portfolio before result export
reason_accepted_or_rejected: REJECTED - all ten standalones negative and matched-entry analysis proves the profit floor clipped the trend winners
notes: V4 standalones: BTC -59.44 PF0.483; ETH -13.76 PF0.927; SOL -19.65 PF0.884; XRP -17.25 PF0.865; BNB -55.23 PF0.636; DOGE -29.98 PF0.802; LINK -61.85 PF0.622; TRX -43.08 PF0.622; LTC -77.15 PF0.450; BCH -83.64 PF0.494. Sum of the ten independent diagnostics was -461.03 USDT but is not a shared-wallet portfolio result. In matched same-entry trades, the V4 stop converted V3A eventual P/L to almost zero: BTC +31.12 -> 0.00, XRP +45.26 -> -0.48, DOGE +70.55 -> +0.18 and TRX +55.39 -> +0.85. ETH's 116 newly admitted no-slope entries lost -24.91 in V4; matching those entries to V1 original exits shows they were also -8.98 USDT without the V4 stop, disproving the ETH slope-removal hypothesis on the full set.
change_summary: Preserve Hixton motor and original lower-band exit; add pair-specific activated fee-covering floor; loosen only ETH from close-above-and-rising to close-above 1h VIDYA.
acceptance_criteria: Improve PF/net P/L across the majority of pairs without materially reducing the large trend winners. DOGE/XRP/TRX should remain positive; ETH/SOL should cross or approach PF>1; BTC/LINK should improve; BNB/LTC/BCH remain diagnostic and must not be declared solved without actual backtest. Shared portfolio must complete before promotion.
result_summary: Eight of ten coins worsened versus V3A; only BNB (+3.88 USDT delta) and LTC (+2.47 delta) improved slightly while remaining deeply negative. The custom stop saved losing trades but destroyed much larger eventual winners. V4 is rejected without waiting for a shared-wallet result.
lessons: Do not use MFE-triggered break-even/profit floors on 15m intrabar highs for this trend follower. Restore the strict native 1h slope for ETH. Preserve proven V3A routes as controls and isolate higher-timeframe experiments to structurally weak pairs.

hypothesis: V4 proved that universal profit protection is destructive. V3A should therefore be restored unchanged for ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE/LINK/TRX. BTC and BNB had positive gross price edge but insufficient edge after fees, so adding a completed bullish/non-falling 4h Hixton context should reduce weak 15m entries. LTC and BCH had negative gross price edge before fees, so moving their Hixton event/exit to native completed 1h candles plus a bullish/non-falling 4h regime should test whether the 15m route itself is the problem.
validation_window: all ten individual diagnostics plus shared 3x80 portfolio
reason_accepted_or_rejected: RESEARCH CANDIDATE - targeted pair routes, no V4 profit floor
notes: Six controls: ETH/SOL/XRP/DOGE/LINK/TRX use the exact V3A 15m flip-up + native 1h bullish/rising guard + original 15m flip-down route. BTC/BNB add completed 4h close above a non-falling 4h VIDYA. LTC/BCH use one-shot completed 1h Hixton flip-up/flip-down events guarded by completed 4h close above non-falling 4h VIDYA. Purchased VIDYA10/momentum20/SMA15/ATR200x2 motor is unchanged on every timeframe.
change_summary: Remove V4 custom stop and ETH exception; restore V3A controls; add 4h guard only to BTC/BNB; switch LTC/BCH to 1h Hixton events plus 4h guard.
acceptance_criteria: Controls should return close to their V3A behaviour and must not show trailing_stop_loss exits. BTC/BNB should materially reduce trade count and improve PF/net expectancy versus V3A. LTC/BCH should materially reduce 15m churn and improve gross and net expectancy; reject their 1h route if PF remains clearly below 1. Shared portfolio must complete before any promotion.
lessons: This is deliberately route-level rather than threshold tuning: positive V3A coins are protected as controls while weak pairs test higher-timeframe hypotheses.
next_experiment: Run the locked 3y ten-coin batch plus shared portfolio; compare the six controls to V3A and the four treatment pairs to both V3A and V4.
